sections.text_helper: Section 48.4.4 "SAES symmetric cipher implementation" in chapter 48 (Secure AES coprocessor (SAES)), RM0486 Rev 4, page 2306.
sections.section_content:
The secure AES coprocessor (SAES) is a 32-bit AHB peripheral that encrypts or decrypts
16-byte blocks of data using the advanced encryption standard (AES). It also implements a
set of approved AES symmetric key security functions summarized in Table403. Those
functions can be certified NIST PUB 140-3.
[Table 403. SAES approved symmetric key functions]
SAES can be used directly by the CPU, or indirectly, using two DMA channels (one for the
plaintext, one for the ciphertext).
It is possible to suspend then resume any SAES processing, following the sequence
described in Section48.4.8.
